# Walk-Forward / Out-of-Sample Report — Gold Command Center

**Analysis only. No live-app changes, no deploy.** Generated by `walk_forward.py`, which imports
and drives the **actual** system code (`app.build_day` for signals/plans, `trade_journal.py` for the
trade engine) — not a re-implementation.

## TL;DR verdict

| Execution model (OOS, rolling windows) | Trades | Win% | **PF** | Total R | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Real trade engine** (4H-close confirm, 1H-touch exit, $0.50 cost) | 89 | 48% | **0.71** | **−2.6** | ❌ **FAILED** |
| ↳ WITH-TREND subset (what the live engine actually gates on) | 60 | 48% | 0.54 | −3.5 | ❌ FAILED |
| **Idealised plan model** (`build_4h_plan`: pivot-**touch** entry, no cost) — *the in-sample PF-1.52 model* | 72 | 61% | **1.43** | **+10.0** | ✅ ROBUST |

**The signal has a real, OOS-stable edge — but ONLY if you can enter at the pivot with low cost. The
way the live trade engine actually executes (confirming entry on the 4H *close*) throws that edge away.**
The single cause is **entry slippage: the fill lands on average $28 past the planned pivot — 70% of the
way to the stop — so 37% of trades that "hit their target" still lose money.**

Filter B makes **no meaningful difference** out-of-sample (PF 0.71 ON vs 0.70 OFF), consistent with its
surgical ~1-trade in-sample footprint.

## 1. Data used (pulled fresh from the Google Sheet via gviz CSV — same path the app uses)

| Tab | Range | Count | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gold_price` (daily spot OHLC) | 2025-01-01 → 2026-06-11 | 375 days | the reliable spine |
| `MOON_REAL` (signs + ingress) | 2025-01-01 → 2026-12-31 | 730 days | 321 days carry an intraday ingress time (TZ unlabeled) |
| `SIGN_LIBRARY` / `MOON_PHASE_LIBRARY` | — | 12 / 8 | static reference |
| **`WEEKLY_FORECAST`** (the user's base signal) | **2026-06-05 → 2026-06-18** | **10 rows** | ⚠️ **nearly empty** — see caveat |
| `H4_DATA` | 2024-11-01 → 2026-06-12 | 3,000 | execution timeframe |
| `H1_DATA` | 2025-01-01 → 2026-06-11 | 10,658 | exit-touch timeframe; **live merge src = `futures` (Yahoo GC=F), no `TWELVEDATA_KEY`** |

**Caveat A — the "sheet signal" barely exists historically.** `WEEKLY_FORECAST` only covers Jun 5–18 2026.
Across all history the signal source was: engine/base **268 days**, decision-day **82**, pullback **16**,
sheet **4**. **So this walk-forward almost entirely tests the `engine.py` astro signal, not the user's
sheet forecast.** Whatever the dashboard shows as "from your sheet" is not what was historically traded.

**Caveat B — H1 is the futures proxy.** `TWELVEDATA_KEY` is not set, so the live-merged recent H1 is
COMEX **futures** (basis-offset from spot). Touch-based exits on recent days use futures levels.

---

## 2. Method

- **Signals/plans:** the real `app.build_day(date)` (sheet → engine → movable pullback → **Filter B** veto
  → decision-day continuation). Entry/stop/target taken straight from the real `plan4h`. The signal and
  plan for date D use only data **before** D (no look-ahead).
- **Execution:** the real `trade_journal.py` engine — entry confirms on a **4H CLOSE** through the zone,
  stop/take exit on **touch** via real H1 candles, trend-break (3 against 4H closes), 3-day time stop,
  honest fills, **$0.50/round-trip cost**.
- **Replay:** one continuous chronological pass from a **6-month warm-up cutoff (2025-07-01)**. Each
  trading day: `build_day` → place the directional signal into the engine → then feed that day's H4+H1
  candles forward. A trade is only ever driven by candles **after** it was placed. Closed trades are then
  bucketed into rolling **1-month** (and **2-month**) test windows by placement date.
- **Filter B ON vs OFF** by toggling the `HARD_DOWN_NET` threshold.
- **Verdict rule:** ROBUST = aggregate PF ≥ 1.2 **and** < 30% losing windows; MARGINAL = PF ≥ 1.0 and
  < 50% losing; else FAILED.

## 3. Results — REAL trade engine (the live "Live Track Record" rules)

**Aggregate (Filter B ON, all directional): 89 trades · 48% win · PF 0.71 · −2.6R · avg −0.029R · max DD −8.9R → FAILED.**

### Per 1-month window
| Window | n | Win% | PF | Total R |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-07 | 6 | 67% | 3.64 | +2.8 |
| 2025-08 | 12 | 25% | 0.15 | −4.7 ❌ |
| 2025-09 | 5 | 40% | 1.23 | +0.2 |
| 2025-10 | 4 | 100% | ∞ | +2.5 |
| 2025-11 | 9 | 56% | 4.04 | +1.5 |
| 2025-12 | 10 | 40% | 1.55 | +0.8 |
| 2026-01 | 5 | 20% | 0.01 | −3.4 ❌ |
| 2026-02 | 3 | 0% | 0.00 | −2.9 ❌ |
| 2026-03 | 11 | 64% | 0.62 | −0.7 ❌ |
| 2026-04 | 10 | 60% | 1.26 | +1.3 |
| 2026-05 | 9 | 56% | 1.15 | +0.4 |
| 2026-06 | 5 | 40% | 0.48 | −0.6 ❌ |

**5 of 12 windows losing (42%).** 2-month windows: PF 0.71, **4 of 6 losing (67%)** → FAILED.

### Why it fails — verified mechanism (not a harness artifact)
- **Avg entry slippage = $27.9** (median $22.4, max $105.2) between the planned pivot and the 4H-close fill.
- That slippage is **70% of the average planned risk ($39.8)** — you're most of the way to your stop before you even fill.
- **68 trades exited at the "take" level, but 25 of them (37%) were LOSSES** — the fill had slipped *past*
  the target, so "hitting the target" booked a loss.
  - Concrete example: BUY planned entry 3288.50, target 3309.34 — but it confirmed (4H close) at **3336.82**,
    already **$27 above the target**. It then traded back to the take (3309.34) and exited at 3333.80 for **−$3.52**.
- Exit-reason mix (ON): take_touch 42, take_gap 26, stop_touch 16, trend_break 5.

**Root structural flaw:** the stop/target are sized off the **unfilled pivot**, but the engine fills at the
**4H close**, which is routinely far past the pivot. The plan and the fill are inconsistent.

| Filter B **OFF** | 88 | 48% | 0.70 | −2.9 |

**Negligible difference** (one trade, ~0.3R). Filter B neither saves nor hurts the system out-of-sample —
exactly consistent with the in-sample finding that it touches only ~1 historical trade plus the Jun-10 live
case. It is a sensible safety rule for the specific Jun-10 failure mode, **not** a performance driver.

## 6. What this DOES and DOESN'T prove

**What it supports:**
- The **astro/engine signal has a genuine, out-of-sample-stable directional edge** *when executed at the
  pivot with low cost* (plan model ROBUST 1.43 OOS across rolling unseen months).
- The **live trade engine's execution model is broken** and gives the edge back — a clear, fixable target.
- **Filter B is performance-neutral** OOS (a safety rule, not an edge).

**What it does NOT prove (honest limits):**
- **Not a pristine out-of-sample test.** The rules are *fixed* (nothing is refit per window), but **Filter B
  and the per-sign findings were designed after seeing the whole dataset** — we can't un-see those choices.
  This measures **stability across rolling/unseen windows and recent robustness**, not a clean OOS.
- **Tiny sample / single regime.** ~17 months, one big up-move then a fall; per-window n is small (3–12
  trades), so individual windows are noisy and PF swings wildly (0.00–4.04).
- **It tests the ENGINE, not the sheet forecast.** `WEEKLY_FORECAST` is nearly empty historically (4 days),
  so the user's actual sheet-based signal is essentially **untested** here.
- **H1 is futures-proxy**, so touch exits on recent data use the wrong instrument (basis error). With
  `TWELVEDATA_KEY` (spot) the engine numbers could shift — direction unknown until re-run.
- **No position sizing / no concurrent-trade cap** modelled; trades can overlap.

---

## 7. Bottom line & recommendations (priority order)

1. **Fix the execution model — this is the whole ballgame.** Either (a) **enter with a limit at the pivot**
   (as the plan model assumes) instead of confirming on the 4H close, **or** (b) if you keep 4H-close
   confirmation, **re-size the stop/target from the ACTUAL fill price**, not the unfilled pivot. Today the
   plan and the fill disagree by ~$28 (70% of risk) — that single mismatch turns a 1.43 system into a 0.71 one.
2. **Set `TWELVEDATA_KEY`** and re-run this report, so exits use **spot** H1 (removes the futures basis error).
3. **Don't trust the dashboard's PF 1.52 / "Live Track Record" optimism** until #1 is fixed — the realistic,
   cost-aware engine is net-negative OOS as it stands.
4. **Decide what the real signal is.** If the sheet `WEEKLY_FORECAST` is meant to be the brain, it must be
   populated historically and re-tested; right now the tested edge is the engine's.
5. **Get more data / out-of-sample time.** 17 months over one regime is too thin to certify anything;
   re-run quarterly as forward data accrues.
6. Filter B can stay (harmless safety), but **don't count it as an edge**.

## UPDATE — limit-at-pivot entry implemented & deployed

The §7 recommendation was tested out-of-sample and **deployed** (`trade_journal.py` entry changed from
4H-close confirmation to a **LIMIT at the pivot**: a 4H candle that touches the pivot fills AT the pivot;
gap-through fills at the open). Everything else unchanged.

| Metric (OOS, real engine, Filter B ON) | Before (4H-close) | After (limit-at-pivot) |
|---|---|---|
| Trades | 89 | 62 |
| Win% | 48% | **68%** |
| **Profit factor** | **0.71** | **2.69** |
| Total R | −2.6 | **+32.5** |
| Avg R / trade | −0.029 | **+0.525** |
| Max drawdown | −8.9R | −3.6R |
| Losing windows (1-mo) | 42% | **17%** |
| Losing windows (2-mo) | 67% | **0%** |
| Avg entry slippage | $27.9 | **$8.1 (median $0)** |
| Verdict | ❌ FAILED | ✅ **ROBUST** |

Filter B remains performance-neutral (ON 2.69 vs OFF 2.69). WITH-TREND subset: PF 2.89.
⚠️ PF 2.69 is likely optimistic (62 trades, single trending regime, futures-proxy H1) — treat as
"clearly fixed and robust across rolling windows", not a guaranteed live edge. Re-run with
`TWELVEDATA_KEY` (spot H1) and as more forward data accrues.
